summary.title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM

details: Prevailing VLA policies route perception and instruction through a multi-billion-parameter LLM (V→L→A), making every policy call slow and memory-hungry and blocking real-time, resource-constrained deployment.
Claim: for execution-level control the instruction only needs to condition how visual evidence guides action, not open-ended generation or planning.

TurboVLA: a V+L→A manipulation policy that removes the LLM from the control pathway — visual observations and the instruction are encoded independently by compact encoders (vision backbone + lightweight text encoder).

Crux: a small stack of bidirectional cross-attention 'fusion' layers directly exchanges information between the vision and language token streams (each conditioning the other), and the fused features plus separately encoded robot state are decoded by an ACT-style transformer into a continuous action chunk in one parallel forward pass, trained by behavior cloning with L1 loss.
DINOv3 ViT-B (LIBERO) / ViT-L (RoboTwin) vision backbone; BERT instruction encoder keeping full token sequence; shared hidden dim d=256.
N=6 bidirectional vision-language interaction layers, initialized from Grounding DINO feature-enhancer weights.
Multi-view visual tokens with positional + camera-view embeddings; robot state injected only at the action decoder.
Action horizon H=12 on LIBERO (7-DoF continuous actions); ~0.2B total params.
Behavior cloning with L1 loss, lr 5e-5, 4x RTX 4090; no auxiliary language-modeling objective and no embodied pretraining beyond the target benchmark.
LIBERO: OpenVLA no_noops RLDS data, single mixed-suite model, 80k steps, 10k warm-up, effective batch 256.
RoboTwin 2.0: clean demonstrations only, single multi-task model over 50 bimanual tasks, 50-step chunks of 14-dim absolute joint positions, 55k steps, batch 192.
LIBERO: 4 suites (Spatial/Object/Goal/Long), 50 rollouts per task (2,000 trials) under the VLA-Adapter rollout protocol.
RoboTwin 2.0: 100 clean-setting rollouts per task under the StarVLA framework, average success over 50 tasks.

Real world: AgileX Piper single arm, wrist + third-person RGB-D, 4 tasks, LIBERO-pretrained then fine-tuned on 4x65 teleop demos for 12.5k steps, 40 trials/task, compared to pi_0.5 under identical data/protocol.
Efficiency metrics (params, peak inference VRAM, latency from multimodal input to an action chunk) measured for all runnable baselines on one RTX 4090, batch size 1.
Capability-oriented VLAs: OpenVLA, pi_0, pi_0.5, UniVLA, CogVLA, Mantis, MM-ACT, VLA-JEPA, VEGA-3D.
Acceleration-oriented: OpenVLA-OFT, Discrete Diffusion VLA; lightweight: SmolVLA, DreamVLA, VLA-Adapter, Evo-1.
Non-VLA / RoboTwin baselines: Diffusion Policy, ACT, DP3, RDT, FlowPolicy, UP-VLA, StarVLA-alpha.
Language conditioning: none vs learned task-ID embedding vs semantic instruction.
Text encoder: BERT vs T5-Small vs SigLIP-Base.
Interaction design: concatenation only, language-queries-visual, visual-queries-language, bidirectional.
Sweeps of interaction depth N ∈ {2,4,6,8} and action horizon H ∈ {8,12,15}.

key_findings.finding: Removing the LLM from the execution pathway can match or beat far larger VLA policies while cutting latency, memory, and parameters by roughly an order of magnitude.
key_findings.evidence: On LIBERO, TurboVLA reaches 97.7% average success with 0.2B params, 0.9 GB inference VRAM and 31.2 ms latency, versus pi_0.5 at 96.9% with 3.4B params, 12.8 GB, 93.6 ms; it also beats VLA-JEPA (97.2%, 2.8B, 108.7 ms) and lightweight baselines VLA-Adapter (97.3%, 87.3 ms) and Evo-1 (94.8%, 137.2 ms).

key_findings.finding: The advantage generalizes to bimanual multi-task control and to a real robot, not just LIBERO.
key_findings.evidence: On RoboTwin 2.0 clean setting, one multi-task 0.4B model gets 60.2% average success over 50 tasks at 43.4 ms, above pi_0.5 (57.0%, 95.6 ms) and StarVLA-alpha (50.3%, 74.9 ms); on four AgileX Piper real-world tasks it attains 92.5/80/90/87.5% success, consistently above pi_0.5 under the same data and protocol.

key_findings.finding: Semantic language input is essential and carries information beyond closed-set task identity.
key_findings.evidence: Dropping language collapses average success from 97.7% to 70.8% (LIBERO-Goal 97.4% -> 11.6%); replacing instructions with a learned task-ID embedding recovers only 95.4%.

key_findings.finding: Bidirectional vision-language cross-attention is the key fusion mechanism; one-way or no interaction is measurably worse.
key_findings.evidence: Average success: 95.2% with plain concatenation, 96.1% language-queries-visual, 96.5% visual-queries-language, 97.7% bidirectional; depth sweep shows N=6 best (93.5% at N=2, 95.7% at N=4, 96.6% at N=8).

key_findings.finding: The design is robust to the choice of lightweight text encoder, supporting the claim that no generative LLM is needed for instruction semantics.
key_findings.evidence: T5-Small reaches 97.1% and SigLIP-Base 95.5% average success versus 97.7% with BERT, at comparable total parameter counts (141.9M-216.9M).
